change.title: Root technical specifications — device definitions 3
change.reason: Replace the property-by-property conversion with concise, authored technical narratives organized around each record’s function, architecture, operating constraints and qualification. Consolidate enumerations into meaningful list values; explain distinct references by role; state repeated facts only once. Keep socket-group content solely in composition history. Canonical RAM and graphics validation parameters, technical caveats, BOMs and version boundaries are preserved. Legacy technical definitions remain for step 5, except the copied unfitted-card graphics removed by this amendment; pricing and commercial entitlement prose are not propagated into the new technical sections. Revised in response to the author’s general feedback across all seven proposals. Author feedback clarification: Artemis, Artemis PRO, Athena and Athena Server are base computers without an installed graphics card. Remove their copied card implementation chapters, parameters and all graphics modes, including the equivalent legacy video blocks and fixed-mode claims. Preserve the host video-slot interface, compatibility lists and installation requirements. Corresponding card records already own the exact removed implementations. Leave integrated Aurelia/Aurelia+ video, all BOMs, version boundaries and the other 16 elements unchanged.

chapters.description:
Logix Aurelia+ — base computer is a slim desktop built around {processor_id}.

The {expansion_bus_bits}-bit expansion interface supports Plug and Execute. Connector space is reserved for a future 32-bit interface; that is not current bus width.

Installed RAM must satisfy the selected configuration, and a monitor must connect to a fitted video provider. Cartridges must match both the software platform and their socket role; external application cartridges are supported.

The {memory_model_id} maps {lower_ram_kib} KiB of lower RAM plus {common_ram_kib} KiB of fixed common RAM at F000–FFFF. The 64 KiB normal view maps lower RAM at 0000–EFFF. Within 7000–EFFF, 4 KiB pages may temporarily expose ROM or video RAM; hidden RAM retains its contents and is restored after service calls.

The {system_controller_id} refreshes every installed bank independently of CPU activity and latches physical DMA bank selections so mapping changes cannot redirect a transfer. The base population uses {ram_bank_count} 8-bit bank, with common RAM included and no parity. Mixed module types are not allowed.

Motherboard ROM contains {firmware_services}. The {video_controller_id} operates display RAM on an independent 8-bit bus; sprite RAM has a further separate 8-bit bus.

{recommended_system_id} supplies the native Z80/CP/M environment. Applications use {application_api_id} and query usable dimensions rather than branching on model names. Native 40 × 25 and 80 × 25 text are available subject to monitor capabilities.

Logix Artemis — base computer is a full desktop built around {processor_id}.

The {expansion_bus_bits}-bit expansion interface supports Plug and Execute. The rear ROM/EEPROM position serves the operating system and the front position serves office/application software. The host provides a dedicated keyed connector for a separately installed, non-hot-swappable video card without consuming a general-purpose slot; buffered data/address, wait/ready and DMA access are provided, but electrical pinout remains open.

Installed RAM must satisfy the selected configuration, and a monitor must connect to a fitted video provider. Cartridges must match both the software platform and their socket role; external application cartridges are supported.

The base computer is supplied without a graphics card. Display capabilities are defined by the card and monitor selected for the complete system.

Two matched 32-bit modules form each capacity bank, selected independently on the shared bus. Fill banks in order; decode and refresh every rank. Replace the population when changing density rather than mixing module types. Cross-host connector and timing qualification remains open. The system RAM limit is {maximum_ram_kib} KiB. No parity or ECC is fitted; adding it requires a separately qualified BOM.

Native ERA/AIONix applications use {application_api_id}. Applications query the capabilities of the separately installed display hardware.

video.mode_discovery: Enumerate controller modes intersected with identified or configured monitor raster capabilities and available buffering/sprite allocations. Reject unsupported downscaling.

memory_layout.mode_exclusivity: Text/font and bitmap allocations are alternative uses of 32 KiB display DRAM. Exclusive 1 KiB sprite SRAM is available in every mode.
memory_layout.font_policy: One shared 256-glyph bank per mode. Font allocation 2048 bytes at 8×8, 4096 at 8×16 or 8×10 (16-byte glyph stride). Font writes affect both pages.
memory_layout.page_flip: Latch selected page during vertical blank; drawing throughput is not guaranteed by double buffering.

display_memory.organization: 16K × 16 bits; ordinary external DRAM, independent display refresh sequencer.

pixel_buffer.location: On video ASIC; SRAM banks with page ownership latches
pixel_buffer.policy: Eight-pixel parallel renderer fills free pages; independent clocked serializer drains ready pages. Two pages per 640-pixel line; prefill before active display; never overwrite displaying pages. Underflow blanks pixels, preserves sync and sets sticky fault.
pixel_buffer.physical_organization: Each 160-byte bank is 40 words × 32 bits. Load eight 4-bit pixels into a separate 32-bit serializer latch every eight dot clocks, then shift at 21.504 MHz. SRAM array reads run at 2.688 MHz, not one read per dot; filler and drain use different banks.

character_row_cache.purpose: Current and next 80-column character/attribute row; separate from 640-byte pixel FIFO.

timing_budget.qualification: At 250 ns conservative DRAM cycle, 80 glyph fetches consume 20 microseconds per active line; 160-byte row prefetch amortizes across 8/10/16 scanlines. Two row caches and 16-bit reads cover text-row transitions. Verify sprites, refresh and bounded host/DMA slots together at voltage/temperature corners; no guaranteed maximum CPU upload rate.

video.arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.
video.monitor_policy: Read capability descriptor before enabling sync. Mono Pro accepts only raster_640_400; integer-scale legacy modes. Old monitors retain their advertised 200-line raster(s), never 640×400. Native 400-line modes require Mono Pro; new 200-line bitmap modes also work on capable older displays. This is display-mode/API compatibility, not Z80 binary compatibility.

pixel_buffer.policy: Eight-pixel parallel renderer fills free pages; independent clocked serializer drains ready pages. Two pages per 640-pixel line; prefill before active display; never overwrite displaying pages. Underflow blanks pixels, preserves sync and sets sticky fault.
pixel_buffer.physical_organization: Each 160-byte bank is 40 words × 32 bits. Load eight 4-bit pixels into a separate 32-bit serializer latch every eight dot clocks, then shift at 21.504 MHz. SRAM array reads run at 2.688 MHz, not one read per dot; filler and drain use different banks.

character_row_cache.purpose: Current and next 80-column character/attribute row; separate from 640-byte pixel FIFO.

timing_budget.qualification: Requalify existing renderer/FIFO and 16-bit DRAM organization for 640x400x2 and 640x200x4, refresh, sprite fetches, list prefetch and host/DMA stalls together. No greater upload throughput is promised by added capacity.

video.arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.
video.monitor_policy: All earlier modes and sprite/host/API features retained subject to monitor capabilities. Color Pro 14 and Mono Pro support the 640x400 raster; older displays retain their declared raster limits. Horizontal-retrace palette lists require explicit monitor capability; otherwise use static/vertical-retrace palette updates. No forced high scan rate on old monitors.
